name: Bengaluru Tenant Security Deposit Withholding
raw_input: I was renting a 2BHK flat in HSR Layout, Bengaluru for 2 years at Rs 28,000/month. I gave 1 lakh rupees as security deposit. I gave proper 1-month notice on 1st October and vacated the flat on 31st October 2024. I cleared all electricity and water bills and handed over keys. Landlord Mr. Ramesh promised to refund the deposit via UPI in 3 days. Now it has been 25 days, he stopped picking my calls, and yesterday he messaged saying he is deducting Rs 45,000 for 'complete house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning'. There was no damage, just normal nail holes for photo frames and standard wear and tear. I have move-in photos, move-out handover video, all rent payment bank statements, and WhatsApp chat where he acknowledged receiving the flat in good condition. How can I get my Rs 45,000 back?

case_dossier.case_title: Security Deposit Refund Dispute – Rs 45,000 Deduction
case_dossier.summary: The tenant vacated a 2BHK flat in HSR Layout after a 2‑year lease, handed over the property in good condition, and was promised a full security deposit refund. The landlord now claims a Rs 45,000 deduction for repainting and polishing, which the tenant disputes.

timeline.event: Tenancy began; tenant paid Rs 1,00,000 security deposit and monthly rent of Rs 28,000.
Tenant gave one‑month notice to vacate the flat.
Tenant vacated, cleared electricity & water bills, handed over keys, and recorded move‑out video.
Landlord promised to refund the full security deposit via UPI within three days.
Landlord messaged tenant stating a deduction of Rs 45,000 for repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning.

evidence_held: Move‑out handover video showing condition of the property
Bank statements showing monthly rent payments and security deposit payment
WhatsApp chat where landlord acknowledged receipt of the flat in good condition
Copy of the rent receipt / payment confirmations
evidence_needed: Signed rental agreement specifying terms for security deposit and permissible deductions
Inventory or condition checklist (if any) signed by both parties at move‑in and move‑out
Written communication (email/WhatsApp) where landlord initially promised full refund
Any estimate or invoice from the landlord for the claimed repainting/marble polishing work
Proof of payment of electricity and water bills (bills or receipts)
A formal demand letter drafted to the landlord requesting the Rs 45,000 refund
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: The tenant possesses strong visual proof of the property's condition, payment records, and direct acknowledgment from the landlord, making the case against the deduction compelling.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing: You have a solid legal right to get back the full security deposit you paid. Under the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 a landlord can keep only the amount that covers actual damage caused by the tenant – ordinary wear and tear, like the natural fading of paint, cannot be charged. The landlord must return the deposit within 30 days after you handed over peaceful possession, and any deduction must be backed by a detailed, item‑by‑item bill. Since you have video proof that the flat was in good condition, a written acknowledgment from the landlord that the handover was satisfactory, and you paid the deposit as per the agreement, the landlord’s claim of a Rs 45,000 deduction for repainting and polishing is unlikely to be justified. This is a civil dispute, not a criminal cheating case, so you can pursue it through the rent‑control authority or a small causes court without needing to file a police FIR.

governing_laws.relevance: Caps security deposit, mandates refund within 30 days, and bars deductions for normal wear and tear. Requires landlord to provide itemised bills for any deduction.
Tenant must keep the property in the condition it was received, subject only to reasonable wear and tear, and is entitled to the return of the deposit on vacating.
Clarifies that failure to refund a deposit is a civil matter, not a criminal cheating offence, unless there was fraudulent intent at the start.

action_options.title: Send Formal Legal Notice
action_options.cost_estimate: Free to minimal (Speed Post/Registered Email cost)
action_options.details: Draft a notice stating: (a) you vacated on 31 Oct 2024, (b) landlord promised full refund, (c) you are entitled to the entire Rs 1,00,000 deposit under Model Tenancy Act, (d) demand the Rs 45,000 deduction be returned with 12% interest for delay, and (e) give 15 days to comply. Send it by registered post and keep a copy of the receipt.

action_options.title: File Grievance on State Rent Authority / Consumer Helpline
action_options.cost_estimate: Zero court fees for disputes up to Rs 5 Lakhs; only nominal portal registration charges if any
action_options.details: Register the complaint on your State Rent Authority’s online portal (or use the National Consumer Helpline 1915). Upload the rental agreement, security‑deposit receipt, move‑in/out photos, video, WhatsApp acknowledgment, and a copy of the legal notice. The authority will issue a notice to the landlord and can order refund with interest.

action_options.title: Petition Before Local Rent Authority / Small Causes Court
action_options.cost_estimate: Nominal filing fee (usually Rs 500‑Rs 1,000 for amounts under Rs 5 Lakhs)
action_options.details: If the landlord does not comply after the authority’s direction, file a petition for recovery of the deposit and interest. You can represent yourself; the court will consider your evidence (photos, video, payment records, notice). The court can order the landlord to pay the Rs 45,000 plus interest and may award a small penalty for wrongful deduction.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You can handle the entire process yourself: drafting the notice, filing on the rent‑authority portal, and appearing before the Rent Authority or Small Causes Court does not require a lawyer. A lawyer becomes necessary only if the dispute escalates to a higher civil court or if you face a complex counter‑claim.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self‑advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

Legal Grounds** 1. **Model Tenancy Act, 2021** – **Section 13, 14 & 21**: - Security deposit shall be **capped** and **refunded within 30 days** of peaceful possession. - Deductions are permissible **only for actual damage** beyond normal wear and tear and must be supported by an **itemised bill**. 2. **Transfer of Property Act, 1882** – **Section 108(B)(m) & (q)**: - The tenant is required to keep the premises in the condition received, subject only to **reasonable wear and tear**. 3. **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Section 318) & IPC Section 420**: - Non‑refund of a security deposit **does not constitute a criminal offence** unless fraudulent intent is proved; the remedy is **civil**. 4. **RBI/Consumer Protection Act, 2019** (as applicable to banking‑related refunds): - Unjustified withholding of funds attracts **interest at 12 % per annum** (as per prevailing statutory rate). --- ### **8. sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Mr. Ramesh, as per Section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act and the Model Tenancy framework, ordinary wear and tear like wall paint aging cannot be deducted from my deposit. I have the handover video and our chat proof. Please refund my balance 45,000 within 7 days.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Dekhiye, aapka Section 108 ka reference aur video sab dekh liya hai, lekin hamare lease agreement mein clearly likha hai ki paint ka kharcha tenant ko hi dena padega – yeh 'ordinary wear and tear' nahi, balki 'damage' ke roop mein aata hai. Company policy ke hisaab se hum sirf Rs 20,000 hi deduct kar sakte hain, baaki Rs 25,000 aapko turant refund kar denge. Aapke 7‑din ke notice ko dhyan mein rakhte hue, aapko poora balance 45,000 nahi mil paayega, lekin 25,000 ka refund aaj se 3 din ke andar transfer kar denge.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: Aapne exact statute (Section 108) aur apne video/chat proof ka zikr kiya, jo landlord ko legally challenge karne ke liye bahut mazboot hai.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Lease agreement ka specific clause (jaise ki damage vs wear‑and‑tear) aur Karnataka Rent Control Act ya RERA ke relevant provisions ka bhi hawala dena chahiye tha, saath hi statutory refund timeline (30 din) ko bhi mention karna chahiye tha.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Mujhe aapke lease agreement ka clause 5.2 dikhaiye jisme deposit deduction ka koi mention nahi, aur aapke 7‑din ke notice ko dhyan mein rakhte hue, turant Rs 45,000 ka poora refund karein.
